A handler receives each stream in its payload as an `InputStream` to read or an `OutputStream` to
write. A handler can also put a stream in its result. The SDK closes or cancels the streams of each
invocation when the handler returns or throws.

<Note>
  The examples use the stream API of the 0.27 SDKs. To call functions with streams, read streams,
  and create pipes, see [Using iii / Streaming](../using-iii/streaming). To move code from the
  channel API, see [Upgrading from 0.26.x](../upgrading/from-0-26-x).
</Note>

## Receive a stream

A stream field in the payload arrives as an `InputStream`. Read it once. For the read operations,
see [Read and write a stream](../using-iii/streaming#read-and-write-a-stream).

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker, type InputStream } from "iii-sdk";

    const worker = registerWorker(process.env.III_URL ?? "ws://localhost:49134");

    worker.registerFunction(
      "files::process",
      async ({ filename, body }: { filename: string; body: InputStream }) => {
        let bytes = 0;
        for await (const chunk of body) bytes += chunk.length;
        return { filename, bytes };
      },
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    from iii import InputStream, register_worker

    worker = register_worker("ws://localhost:49134")


    async def process(payload: dict) -> dict:
        body: InputStream = payload["body"]
        total = 0
        async for chunk in body:
            total += len(chunk)
        return {"filename": payload["filename"], "bytes": total}


    worker.register_function("files::process", process)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::{Error, InputStream, RegisterFunction};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    use serde_json::json;

    // A typed field: the stream binds to this worker on first read
    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct Upload {
        filename: String,
        body: InputStream,
    }

    worker.register_function(
        "files::process",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(|upload: Upload| async move {
            let bytes = upload.body.read_all().await?.len();
            Ok::<_, Error>(json!({ "filename": upload.filename, "bytes": bytes }))
        }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    // The payload unmarshals into a struct, and the field into an *iii.InputStream
    type upload struct {
    	Filename string           `json:"filename"`
    	Body     *iii.InputStream `json:"body"`
    }

    iii.RegisterFunctionTyped(worker, "files::process", func(ctx context.Context, in upload) (map[string]any, error) {
    	bytes, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, in.Body) // an InputStream is an io.Reader
    	if err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	return map[string]any{"filename": in.Filename, "bytes": bytes}, nil
    })
    ```

  </Tab>

Finish all reads before the handler returns. When the handler returns, the SDK cancels an
`InputStream` that the handler started to read and did not finish. See
[Control the lifecycle](#control-the-lifecycle).

## Return a stream

Put the stream in the result. The caller receives the field as an `InputStream`. The handler's SDK
writes the data into the pipe after the handler returns. The values that the SDK sends as streams
are the same as in a payload: see
[Send a stream in a call](../using-iii/streaming#send-a-stream-in-a-call).

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    async function* csvLines(reportId: string) {
      yield "id,total\n";
      for await (const row of db.rows(reportId)) yield `${row.id},${row.total}\n`;
    }

    worker.registerFunction("reports::export", async ({ report_id }: { report_id: string }) => ({
      report_id,
      csv: csvLines(report_id), // an async generator, a Readable, or a Web ReadableStream
    }));
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python

        yield b"id,total\n"
        async for row in db.rows(report_id):
            yield f"{row.id},{row.total}\n".encode()

    async def export(payload: dict) -> dict:
        return {"report_id": payload["report_id"], "csv": csv_lines(payload["report_id"])}


    worker.register_function("reports::export", export)
    ```

  </Tab>

        "reports::export",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(|req: ExportRequest| async move {
            let lines = db
                .rows(req.report_id.clone())
                .map_ok(|row| Bytes::from(format!("{},{}\n", row.id, row.total)));
            Ok::<_, Error>(Export { report_id: req.report_id, csv: InputStream::from_stream(lines) })
        }),

    })

The worker that returns the stream owns its pipe. Keep the worker connected until the caller has
read the stream.

## Write to a received OutputStream

When the caller passes a sink, the handler receives it as an `OutputStream`. The caller's call
resolves after the sink has received all the data. A sink receives bytes only, so write the data
with `write`.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import type { OutputStream } from "iii-sdk";

    worker.registerFunction(
      "reports::render-pdf",
      async ({ report_id, out }: { report_id: string; out: OutputStream }) => {
        for await (const page of renderPages(report_id)) await out.write(page);
        // Returning closes `out`. Throwing aborts it, so the caller gets an error, not a short file.
      },
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    from iii import OutputStream

    async def render_pdf(payload: dict) -> None:
        out: OutputStream = payload["out"]
        async for page in render_pages(payload["report_id"]):
            await out.write(page)
        # Returning closes `out`. Raising aborts it, so the caller gets an error, not a short file.


    worker.register_function("reports::render-pdf", render_pdf)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use futures::TryStreamExt;
    use iii_sdk::{Error, OutputStream, RegisterFunction};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct RenderPdf {
        report_id: String,
        out: OutputStream,
    }

    worker.register_function(
        "reports::render-pdf",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(|req: RenderPdf| async move {
            let mut pages = render_pages(&req.report_id);
            while let Some(page) = pages.try_next().await? {
                req.out.write(&page).await?;
            }
            // Ok closes `out`. Err aborts it, so the caller gets an error, not a short file.
            Ok::<_, Error>(())
        }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    type renderPDF struct {
    	ReportID string            `json:"report_id"`
    	Out      *iii.OutputStream `json:"out"`
    }

    worker.RegisterFunction("reports::render-pdf", func(ctx context.Context, data json.RawMessage) (any, error) {
    	var req renderPDF
    	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &req); err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	for _, page := range renderPages(req.ReportID) {
    		if err := req.Out.Write(ctx, page); err != nil {
    			return nil, err
    		}
    	}
    	// Returning closes Out. An error aborts it, so the caller gets an error, not a short file.
    	return nil, nil
    })
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

If the caller's sink fails, the next `write` fails with `STREAM_CLOSED`.

## Send messages

`send` serializes a value to JSON and sends it as one text frame. A stream can carry messages and
bytes together. For example, the HTTP worker reads the status and the headers of a route's
`response` as messages, and the body as bytes.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import type { OutputStream } from "iii-sdk";

    type Download = { path_params: { id: string }; response: OutputStream };

    worker.registerFunction("reports::download", async ({ path_params, response }: Download) => {
      // Messages: the HTTP worker reads the status and the headers from text frames
      await response.send({ type: "set_status", status_code: 200 });
      await response.send({ type: "set_headers", headers: { "content-type": "text/csv" } });
      // Bytes: the body
      for await (const line of csvLines(path_params.id)) await response.write(line);
      // Returning closes the response, which ends the body.
    });

    worker.observe(
      { function_id: "http::on-request", args: { method: "GET", path: "/reports/:id/csv" } },
      "reports::download",
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    from iii import OutputStream

    async def download(req: dict) -> None:
        response: OutputStream = req["response"]
        # Messages: the HTTP worker reads the status and the headers from text frames
        await response.send({"type": "set_status", "status_code": 200})
        await response.send({"type": "set_headers", "headers": {"content-type": "text/csv"}})
        # Bytes: the body
        async for line in csv_lines(req["path_params"]["id"]):
            await response.write(line)
        # Returning closes the response, which ends the body.


    worker.register_function("reports::download", download)
    worker.observe(
        {"function_id": "http::on-request", "args": {"method": "GET", "path": "/reports/:id/csv"}},
        "reports::download",
    )
    ```

  </Tab>

    use std::collections::HashMap;

    use iii_sdk::{Error, OutputStream, RegisterFunction, Source};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct Download {
        path_params: HashMap<String, String>,
        response: OutputStream,
    }

    worker.register_function(
        "reports::download",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(|req: Download| async move {
            // Messages: the HTTP worker reads the status and the headers from text frames
            req.response.send(&json!({ "type": "set_status", "status_code": 200 })).await?;
            req.response
                .send(&json!({ "type": "set_headers", "headers": { "content-type": "text/csv" } }))
                .await?;
            // Bytes: the body
            let csv = render_csv(&req.path_params["id"]).await?;
            req.response.write(csv.as_bytes()).await?;
            // Ok closes the response, which ends the body.
            Ok::<_, Error>(())
        }),
    );

    worker.observe(
        Source::function("http::on-request").args(json!({ "method": "GET", "path": "/reports/:id/csv" })),
        "reports::download",
    );

  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    type download struct {
    	PathParams map[string]string `json:"path_params"`
    	Response   *iii.OutputStream `json:"response"`
    }

    worker.RegisterFunction("reports::download", func(ctx context.Context, data json.RawMessage) (any, error) {
    	var req download
    	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &req); err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	// Messages: the HTTP worker reads the status and the headers from text frames
    	if err := req.Response.Send(ctx, map[string]any{"type": "set_status", "status_code": 200}); err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	headers := map[string]any{"type": "set_headers", "headers": map[string]string{"content-type": "text/csv"}}
    	if err := req.Response.Send(ctx, headers); err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	// Bytes: the body
    	for _, line := range csvLines(req.PathParams["id"]) {
    		if err := req.Response.Write(ctx, []byte(line)); err != nil {
    			return nil, err
    		}
    	}
    	// Returning closes the response, which ends the body.
    	return nil, nil
    })

    worker.Observe(iii.Source{
    	FunctionID: "http::on-request",
    	Args:       iii.Args{"method": "GET", "path": "/reports/:id/csv"},
    }, "reports::download")
    ```

## Forward a stream

A handler can put a received stream in another call without reading it. An unread `InputStream`
travels as its ref, so no data goes through the forwarding worker.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import type { HttpRequest } from "@iii-dev/helpers/http";

    worker.registerFunction("files::upload", async (req: HttpRequest) => {
      // request_body is an InputStream: pass it on without reading it
      const result = await worker.call({
        function_id: "files::process",
        payload: { filename: req.path_params.name, body: req.request_body },
      });
      return { status_code: 200, body: result };
    });

    worker.observe(
      { function_id: "http::on-request", args: { method: "PUT", path: "/files/:name" } },
      "files::upload",
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    async def upload(req: dict) -> dict:
        # request_body is an InputStream: pass it on without reading it
        result = await worker.call_async(
            {
                "function_id": "files::process",
                "payload": {"filename": req["path_params"]["name"], "body": req["request_body"]},
            }
        )
        return {"status_code": 200, "body": result}

    worker.register_function("files::upload", upload)
    worker.observe(
        {"function_id": "http::on-request", "args": {"method": "PUT", "path": "/files/:name"}},
        "files::upload",
    )
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    use iii_sdk::{CallRequest, Error, InputStream, RegisterFunction, Source};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct PutFile {
        path_params: HashMap<String, String>,
        request_body: InputStream,
    }

    let client = worker.clone();
    worker.register_function(
        "files::upload",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(move |req: PutFile| {
            let client = client.clone();
            async move {
                // request_body is an InputStream: pass it on without reading it
                let result = client
                    .call(CallRequest::new(
                        "files::process",
                        json!({ "filename": req.path_params["name"], "body": req.request_body }),
                    ))
                    .await?;
                Ok::<_, Error>(json!({ "status_code": 200, "body": result }))
            }
        }),
    );

    worker.observe(
        Source::function("http::on-request").args(json!({ "method": "PUT", "path": "/files/:name" })),
        "files::upload",
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    // iiihttp is github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii/helpers/http
    iii.RegisterFunctionTyped(worker, "files::upload", func(ctx context.Context, req iiihttp.Request[json.RawMessage]) (map[string]any, error) {
    	// RequestBody is an *iii.InputStream: pass it on without reading it
    	payload, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
    		"filename": req.PathParams["name"],
    		"body":     req.RequestBody,
    	})
    	if err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	result, err := worker.Call(ctx, iii.CallRequest{FunctionID: "files::process", Payload: payload})
    	if err != nil {
    		return nil, err
    	}
    	return map[string]any{"status_code": 200, "body": result}, nil
    })

    worker.Observe(iii.Source{
    	FunctionID: "http::on-request",
    	Args:       iii.Args{"method": "PUT", "path": "/files/:name"},
    }, "files::upload")
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

An `OutputStream` that the handler has not used travels as its ref too. When the handler has read
from the stream, or has built the stream itself, the forwarding worker sends the data itself.
Forwarding does not change the owner of the pipe.

## Abort a stream

An abort tells the reader that the stream is incomplete. The reader receives the data sent before
the abort, and then an error with the code `STREAM_ABORTED`. A stream aborts when:

- The source that the SDK reads from throws, for example a failed generator.
- The handler throws after it used an `OutputStream` it received.
- The handler calls `abort(reason)`. If the socket of the stream is not open, `abort` opens it
  first, so the reader always gets the error.
- The worker crashes or loses its connection.

The engine does not send the reason to the reader. The reader gets the engine's text, for example
`channel writer aborted: closed with code 1011`. Only a call that the SDK runs in the same process
keeps the reason. To tell the caller the cause, fail the call or put the cause in its result.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    // Fail the stream, and still answer the call with the cause
    try {
      for await (const page of renderPages(report_id)) await out.write(page);
    } catch (err) {
      await out.abort(`render failed: ${String(err)}`);
      return { ok: false, error: String(err) };
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    # Fail the stream, and still answer the call with the cause
    try:
        async for page in render_pages(report_id):
            await out.write(page)
    except Exception as err:
        await out.abort(f"render failed: {err}")
        return {"ok": False, "error": str(err)}
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    // Fail the stream, and still answer the call with the cause
    if let Err(err) = render_into(&req.out).await {
        req.out.abort(format!("render failed: {err}")).await?;
        return Ok(json!({ "ok": false, "error": err.to_string() }));
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    // Fail the stream, and still answer the call with the cause
    if err := renderInto(ctx, req.Out); err != nil {
    	_ = req.Out.Abort("render failed: " + err.Error())
    	return map[string]any{"ok": false, "error": err.Error()}, nil
    }
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For the errors a reader gets, see
[Handle aborts and errors](../using-iii/streaming#handle-aborts-and-errors).

## Control the lifecycle

When the handler returns or throws, the SDK closes or cancels the streams that the handler received.
The common path needs no cleanup code.

| When the handler            | An `OutputStream` it received                           | An `InputStream` it received                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| returns, after it used it   | is closed                                               | is cancelled if the handler did not finish it |
| throws, after it used it    | is aborted                                              | is cancelled if the handler did not finish it |
| returns, and did not use it | is closed, so the caller's sink ends with no data       | is not changed                                |
| throws, and did not use it  | is not changed                                          | is not changed                                |
| put it in another call      | is not changed: the function that received it closes it | is not changed                                |

To use an `OutputStream` is to write to it, send on it, or take its native API. To use an
`InputStream` is to start any read.

When the SDK cancels an `InputStream`, the engine closes its writer. A read that is still running
then, for example in a task the handler started, fails with `STREAM_CLOSED`. There is no way to keep
a received `InputStream` open after the handler returns.

Calls that the SDK sends to a function in the same worker follow the same rules, in the process and
without a pipe.

### Calls through an observer

In a call through an observer, the SDK closes an unused `OutputStream` only when the handler returns
nothing (`null`). When the handler returns a value, the SDK does not change the stream. The source
of the event sets what an unused stream means. For example, the HTTP worker calls a route through an
observer, and sends an unused `response` together with the result as a buffered response.

If a worker calls through an observer with its own sink, and the target returns a value without
using the sink, the call fails with `TIMEOUT` when its timeout expires.

### Keep writing after the handler returns

Call `keepOpen()` before the handler returns. Then close or abort the stream yourself.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import type { OutputStream } from "iii-sdk";

    worker.registerFunction(
      "jobs::start",
      async ({ job_id, log }: { job_id: string; log: OutputStream }) => {
        log.keepOpen(); // this handler answers now and keeps writing
        void (async () => {
          try {
            for await (const line of runJob(job_id)) await log.write(`${line}\n`);
            await log.close();
          } catch (err) {
            await log.abort(String(err));
          }
        })();
        return { started: true };
      },
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import asyncio

    from iii import OutputStream

    running: set[asyncio.Task] = set()


    async def start(payload: dict) -> dict:
        log: OutputStream = payload["log"]
        log.keep_open()  # this handler answers now and keeps writing

        async def write_log() -> None:
            async with log:  # closes on exit, aborts on an exception
                async for line in run_job(payload["job_id"]):
                    await log.write(f"{line}\n")

        task = asyncio.create_task(write_log())
        running.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(running.discard)
        return {"started": True}


    worker.register_function("jobs::start", start)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct StartJob {
        job_id: String,
        log: OutputStream,
    }

    worker.register_function(
        "jobs::start",
        RegisterFunction::new_async(|req: StartJob| async move {
            req.log.keep_open(); // this handler answers now and keeps writing
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                match run_job(&req.job_id, &req.log).await {
                    Ok(()) => req.log.close().await,
                    Err(err) => req.log.abort(err.to_string()).await,
                }
            });
            Ok::<_, Error>(json!({ "started": true }))
        }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go">
    ```go
    type startJob struct {
    	JobID string            `json:"job_id"`
    	Log   *iii.OutputStream `json:"log"`
    }

    iii.RegisterFunctionTyped(worker, "jobs::start", func(ctx context.Context, req startJob) (map[string]bool, error) {
    	req.Log.KeepOpen() // this handler answers now and keeps writing
    	go func() {
    		if err := runJob(ctx, req.JobID, req.Log); err != nil {
    			_ = req.Log.Abort(err.Error())
    			return
    		}
    		_ = req.Log.Close()
    	}()
    	return map[string]bool{"started": true}, nil
    })
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

When the caller passed a sink, the call resolves only after the stream ends.

## Payload size

The JSON message limit applies to the complete serialized UTF-8 JSON envelope, in bytes. For more
data, use a stream: only its ref counts toward the limit. See
[Send a stream in a call](../using-iii/streaming#send-a-stream-in-a-call).

### Limits

| Sender or receiver                | Limit                                     |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Rust, Node, Python, and Go SDKs   | **64 MiB**                                |
| Browser SDK                       | **16 MiB** to send, **16 MiB** to receive |
| Engine, per message from a worker | **64 MiB**                                |

The Rust, Node, Python, and Go SDKs send a message of up to **16 MiB** as one text frame. They send
a larger message, up to and including 64 MiB, as one fragmented WebSocket text message. The browser
SDK does not fragment messages, because browser WebSocket APIs give no frame control.

The engine sends each message larger than **1 MiB** to a worker as a fragmented text message of 1
MiB frames, so no frame exceeds the frame size limit of a worker. The engine accepts one message as
one frame or as fragments, so it also accepts the large single frames of SDKs before 0.24.5. The
function APIs do not change.

### Receive limit of a worker

The engine checks each message against the receive limit of the target worker. When the target
cannot accept the message, the engine returns `payload_too_large` to the caller. The engine sets the
limit when the worker registers:

- A browser worker gets **16 MiB**.
- A worker that declares the `large-messages.v1` protocol feature gets **64 MiB**, for any version
  it reports. The Rust, Node, Python, and Go SDKs declare it from 0.25.0. The browser SDK does not.
- Any other worker gets **64 MiB** when it reports an SDK version of 0.24.5 or later, as semver
  (`0.24.6`, `0.25.0-rc.5`) or PEP 440 (`0.25.0rc5`, `0.24.5.post1`). It gets **16 MiB** when the
  version is missing, cannot be parsed, or is older, including pre-releases of 0.24.5. Other
  features, such as `observe.v1`, do not count.

SDK 0.24.5 through 0.25.0-rc.5 do not declare `large-messages.v1`, so the engine uses the version
they report. A Rust worker on one of these SDKs that sets `WorkerMetadata.version` to its own
version stays at 16 MiB. Upgrade it to SDK 0.25.0 or later.

### Messages over the limit

- Above **64 MiB**, the Rust, Node, Python, and Go SDKs refuse the message before they send it, with
  `payload_too_large`. The error message links to this section.
- The engine drops a message over 64 MiB from a worker, and the connection stays open. A call gets
  `payload_too_large` as its result. When a result is too large, the caller gets
  `payload_too_large`. Other calls on the connection continue. The engine drops and logs a message
  that it cannot answer, such as a call that expects no result.
- Engines before the receive limit check send a message as one frame, and do not check the limit of
  the target. An older worker can then disconnect. Use an engine and SDKs from the same release, or
  newer.

Observer activations have the same limits. The engine keeps at most **64 MiB** of one observed
event: every field that its observers capture, with input and output counted separately. The engine
does not deliver an event over either limit: the observer counts a `TOO_LARGE` drop and the engine
logs a warning. See [Observers / Observed call size](../using-iii/observers#observed-call-size).

## Go and the browser SDK

The Go SDK and the browser SDK differ from the TypeScript SDK in these points.

In Go:

- Reads take a `context.Context`, except `Read`, which makes an `InputStream` an `io.Reader`.
- `Lines`, `Messages`, and `Frames` are iterators. To exit the loop early cancels the stream.
- After a failed read, each later read returns the same error.
- The HTTP helpers in `github.com/iii-hq/iii/sdk/packages/go/iii/helpers/http` wrap the streams of a
  route. `iiihttp.Wrap(fn)` gives the handler a `StreamRequest`, an `io.Reader` over `request_body`,
  and a `StreamResponse` with `Status`, `Headers`, and `Write`. The SDK closes or aborts the
  response by the lifecycle rules.

In the browser:

- The API is the TypeScript API, with Web streams only. Sources are `ReadableStream`, `Blob` and
  `File`, async generators, and `InputStream`. Sinks are `WritableStream` and `OutputStream`.
  `InputStream.from(...)` also takes an `ArrayBuffer`. The native API is `toWebStream()` only.
- The ref helpers are in `iii-browser-sdk/protocol`.
- An abort closes the socket of the stream with code 4011, because a browser can send only 1000 or a
  code from 3000 to 4999. The engine treats 4011 as an abort, so the reader's `reason` is
  `channel writer aborted: closed with code 4011`.
- `write` resolves when the socket holds 1 MiB or less of unsent data. `close()` waits until that
  buffer is empty.
- Reads have no backpressure. A page cannot pause its socket, so frames that arrive before the page
  reads them stay in memory. Read a stream as it arrives, or cancel it.
- The socket of a stream keeps the query of the engine URL, such as `?token=`.

Streams cross between all SDKs and between 0.26 and 0.27 SDKs. See
[Old and new SDKs](../using-iii/streaming#old-and-new-sdks).
